gpt.text:
Run the three “Next Commands” in order. Here’s what each does, what artifacts to check, and a couple quick sanity checks before/after.

## 0) Quick preflight (recommended)
```bash
git status
python3 --version
ls -lah baseline/champion_v5_latest.json
```
- Ensure working tree is clean (or at least you know what’s modified).
- Confirm the champion file exists.

## 1) AUB autopilot: run + select best
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --run --select-best
```
What to look for:
- It should execute candidate runs from the module registry, score them, and if a candidate beats the current champion it will update the “champion” selection (often by writing a new champion json or updating the pointer file depending on your repo conventions).
- After it completes, re-check:
  ```bash
  ls -lah baseline/champion_v5_latest.json
  git diff -- baseline/champion_v5_latest.json
  ```
  If the champion changed, you should see a diff.

If it reports no PASS candidates: that’s consistent with your handoff (“Last PASS Candidate: none”).

## 2) System autopilot: run system-level candidates
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py \
  --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml --run
```
What to look for:
- This typically evaluates end-to-end/system configurations (not just module tweaks).
- Expect a run log plus result summaries somewhere under `baseline/reports/` or a run output directory used by your framework.

After it completes, search for new reports:
```bash
find baseline/reports -maxdepth 2 -type f -name "*.md" -o -name "*.json" | sort
```

## 3) Generate “next fix” plan
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```
Then open:
```bash
sed -n '1,200p' baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```
This should propose the next targeted fix(es) based on latest failures/near-misses.

## If you paste back outputs
If you paste:
- the tail of each command’s stdout/stderr (last ~100 lines), and
- any newly generated summary file paths,

I can help interpret whether a new champion was selected, why candidates failed, and what to prioritize from `next_fix.md`.
